covers: INT 21h, the DOS services: every function and subfunction the emulator's DOS_21Handler has a case for, except the Windows-only named-pipe calls of AH=5Fh.

entries.name: terminate program
entries.description: Ends the program with return code 00h; DOS 2+ programs should use AH=4Ch instead.
entries.behaviour: CS is the PSP segment. The emulator passes DOS_Terminate the PSP segment it reads from the stack word above the return IP (the caller's CS), with return code 0, and clears the running program's name and arguments. If SP is above 0xFFFA it pops IP, CS and flags and uses the popped CS.

entries.name: read char echo
entries.description: Reads one character from standard input and echoes it to standard output, checking for ^C.
entries.behaviour: Returns the character in AL. A ^C (3) runs the break action, and the call returns with no result if the break test then fails. Under DOS 2+ the character is written to STDOUT; when emulating DOS 1 an echo flag is set during the read instead.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - READ CHARACTER FROM STANDARD INPUT, WITH ECHO
case 0x01:      /* Read character from STDIN, with echo */

entries.name: write char
entries.description: Writes the character in DL to standard output.
entries.behaviour: Returns AL = the character written, although the official docs say nothing is returned. A tab (09h) is expanded to blanks, so AL is 20h in that case. The emulator writes DL to STDOUT and sets AL to 20h when DL is 9, else to DL.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - WRITE CHARACTER TO STANDARD OUTPUT

entries.name: read aux char
entries.description: Reads one character from the auxiliary device, usually the first serial port.
entries.behaviour: Returns the character in AL. The emulator reads the port base from the word at 0040:0000; if it is nonzero and the first serial port exists, it writes 3 to base+4 (RTS and DTR on) and waits for a character. Otherwise AL is left unchanged.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - READ CHARACTER FROM STDAUX

entries.name: write aux char
entries.description: Writes the character in DL to the auxiliary device, usually the first serial port.
entries.behaviour: The emulator reads the port base from the word at 0040:0000; if it is nonzero and the first serial port exists, it writes 3 to base+4 (RTS and DTR on), sends DL, then writes 1 to base+4 (RTS off). Otherwise it does nothing.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - WRITE CHARACTER TO STDAUX

entries.name: write printer char
entries.description: Writes the character in DL to the standard printer, usually the first parallel port.
entries.behaviour: The emulator sends DL to the first of the first three parallel ports that exists, and does nothing if none does.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - WRITE CHARACTER TO PRINTER

entries.name: direct console io
entries.description: Writes the character in DL to standard output without checking ^C; with DL=FFh it reads a character instead.
entries.behaviour: With DL=FFh: ZF clear and AL = the character, or ZF set and AL=00h if none is available; an overhead delay is simulated. Otherwise DL is written to STDOUT and AL = DL (the docs say nothing is returned). ^C is not checked.

entries.name: direct char input
entries.description: Reads one character from standard input without echo and without checking ^C.
entries.behaviour: Returns the character in AL. The emulator reads one byte from STDIN into AL and does no break check.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - DIRECT CHARACTER INPUT, WITHOUT ECHO

entries.name: read char no echo
entries.description: Reads one character from standard input without echoing it, checking for ^C.
entries.behaviour: Returns the character in AL. A ^C (3) runs the break action, and the call returns with no result if the break test fails; when STDIN is a redirected regular file the ^C byte is skipped and the next one read. At end of input AL is 0.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - CHARACTER INPUT WITHOUT ECHO
case 0x08:      /* Direct Character Input, without echo (checks for breaks officially :)*/

entries.name: write string
entries.description: Writes the '$'-terminated string at DS:DX to standard output.
entries.behaviour: Returns AL = 24h, the '$' (the docs say nothing is returned). The emulator writes each byte from DS:DX up to the '$' to STDOUT. It skips the write when the string is one of the Windows-only program notices (such as 'This program cannot be run in DOS mode.') and its winautorun and startquiet settings call for it.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - WRITE STRING TO STANDARD OUTPUT

entries.name: buffered input
entries.description: Reads a line of input into the buffer at DS:DX, whose first byte is its capacity.
entries.behaviour: Byte 0 is the maximum size (nothing is read if it is 0), byte 1 receives the count of characters read excluding CR, and the characters follow from byte 2, including the final CR. The emulator echoes each character, handles backspace and rings the bell when full. Redirected input that reaches end of file stops the emulator with an error.

entries.name: stdin status
entries.description: Reports whether a character is waiting on standard input.
entries.behaviour: Returns AL=FFh if a character is available and 00h if not. The emulator adds a simulated DOS overhead for timing-sensitive programs.

entries.name: flush and read
entries.description: Empties the standard input buffer, then runs the input function AL names.
entries.behaviour: AL = 01h, 06h, 07h, 08h or 0Ah selects the input function run after the flush, with the registers it takes; any other AL flushes only, and the emulator returns AL=0. The emulator flushes only when STDIN is the CON device.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - FLUSH BUFFER AND READ STANDARD INPUT
case 0x0c:      /* Flush Buffer and read STDIN call */

entries.name: flush, read char echo
entries.description: Flushes standard input, then runs AH=01h.
entries.behaviour: The emulator reads and discards pending STDIN input when STDIN is the CON device, then runs its AH=01h handler with the same registers and restores AH afterwards.

entries.name: flush, direct console
entries.description: Flushes standard input, then runs AH=06h.
entries.behaviour: The emulator reads and discards pending STDIN input when STDIN is the CON device, then runs its AH=06h handler with the same registers and restores AH afterwards.

entries.name: flush, direct input
entries.description: Flushes standard input, then runs AH=07h.
entries.behaviour: The emulator reads and discards pending STDIN input when STDIN is the CON device, then runs its AH=07h handler with the same registers and restores AH afterwards.

entries.name: flush, read no echo
entries.description: Flushes standard input, then runs AH=08h.
entries.behaviour: The emulator reads and discards pending STDIN input when STDIN is the CON device, then runs its AH=08h handler with the same registers and restores AH afterwards.

entries.name: flush, buffered input
entries.description: Flushes standard input, then runs AH=0Ah.
entries.behaviour: The emulator reads and discards pending STDIN input when STDIN is the CON device, then runs its AH=0Ah handler with the same registers and restores AH afterwards.

entries.name: disk reset
entries.description: Asks DOS to write all modified disk buffers to disk.
entries.behaviour: The emulator's handler does nothing: no buffer is written, and no register or flag is changed.
entries.differs: The list says it writes all modified disk buffers to disk; the emulator's handler does nothing.

entries.name: set drive
entries.description: Makes the drive in DL the default drive and returns how many drives may be valid.
entries.behaviour: DL = drive (00h = A:, 01h = B:). The emulator sets the default drive to DL, then returns AL = its maxdrive value (1 if outside 1 to 26), raised to the number of the highest mounted drive.
entries.differs: The list gives AL as the greatest of 5, LASTDRIVE and the drives present under DOS 3.0+; the emulator uses its own maxdrive value and the highest mounted drive.

entries.name: fcb open
entries.description: Opens the file named by the unopened FCB at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the FCB. The emulator passes DS and DX to DOS_FCBOpen and returns AL=00h on success and FFh on failure.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - OPEN FILE USING FCB

entries.name: fcb close
entries.description: Closes the file of the opened FCB at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the FCB. The emulator passes DS and DX to DOS_FCBClose and returns AL=00h on success and FFh on failure.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - CLOSE FILE USING FCB

entries.name: fcb find first
entries.description: Finds the first file matching the FCB at DS:DX, which may hold wildcards.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the FCB. The emulator passes DS and DX to DOS_FCBFindFirst and returns AL=00h if a match was found and FFh if not.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - FIND FIRST MATCHING FILE USING FCB
case 0x11:      /* Find First Matching File using FCB */

entries.name: fcb find next
entries.description: Finds the next file matching the search FCB at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the FCB. The emulator passes DS and DX to DOS_FCBFindNext and returns AL=00h if a match was found and FFh if not.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - FIND NEXT MATCHING FILE USING FCB
case 0x12:      /* Find Next Matching File using FCB */

entries.name: fcb delete
entries.description: Deletes the files matching the FCB at DS:DX, which may hold wildcards.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the FCB. The emulator passes DS and DX to DOS_FCBDeleteFile and returns AL=00h on success and FFh on failure.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - DELETE FILE USING FCB

entries.name: fcb create
entries.description: Creates or truncates the file named by the unopened FCB at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the FCB. The emulator passes DS and DX to DOS_FCBCreate and returns AL=00h on success and FFh on failure.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - CREATE OR TRUNCATE FILE USING FCB
case 0x16:      /* Create or truncate file using FCB */

entries.name: fcb rename
entries.description: Renames the files matching the modified FCB at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the FCB. The emulator passes DS and DX to DOS_FCBRenameFile and returns AL=00h on success and FFh on failure.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - RENAME FILE USING FCB

entries.name: fcb sequential read
entries.description: Reads the next record of the opened FCB at DS:DX into the disk transfer area.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the FCB. AL is the status DOS_FCBRead returns: 00h successful, 01h no data, 03h partial record read.
entries.differs: The list also gives 02h, segment wrap in the DTA; the FCB helpers in src/dos/dos_files.cpp (FCB_SUCCESS, FCB_READ_NODATA, FCB_READ_PARTIAL) never return it.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - SEQUENTIAL READ FROM FCB FILE

entries.name: fcb sequential write
entries.description: Writes the record in the disk transfer area to the opened FCB at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the FCB. AL is the status DOS_FCBWrite returns: 00h successful, 01h for any failure.
entries.differs: The list gives 01h as disk full and also 02h, segment wrap in the DTA; the FCB helpers in src/dos/dos_files.cpp return 01h (FCB_ERR_WRITE) for every failure and never 02h.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - SEQUENTIAL WRITE TO FCB FILE

entries.name: null: logged drives
entries.description: Does nothing: it stands in for the CP/M call for the map of logged drives.
entries.behaviour: The emulator sends it to its default case, which sets AL to 00h and logs the call as unhandled.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - NULL FUNCTION FOR CP/M COMPATIBILITY
case 0x18:      /* NULL Function for CP/M compatibility or Extended rename FCB */

entries.name: get drive
entries.description: Returns the current default drive.
entries.behaviour: Returns AL = drive (00h = A:, 01h = B:). The emulator reads it with DOS_GetDefaultDrive.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - GET CURRENT DEFAULT DRIVE

entries.name: set dta
entries.description: Sets the disk transfer area to DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the new disk transfer area. The emulator stores the segment of DS and the offset DX as the current DTA.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - SET DISK TRANSFER AREA ADDRESS
case 0x1a:      /* Set Disk Transfer Area Address */

entries.name: drive info default
entries.description: Returns the allocation information of the default drive.
entries.behaviour: Returns AL = sectors per cluster, CX = bytes per sector, DX = total clusters, and DS:BX -> the media ID byte, as the list gives; AL=FFh if DOS_GetAllocationInfo fails.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - GET ALLOCATION INFORMATION FOR DEFAULT DRIVE
case 0x1b:      /* Get allocation info for default drive */

entries.name: drive info
entries.description: Returns the allocation information of the drive in DL.
entries.behaviour: DL = drive (00h = default, 01h = A:). Returns AL = sectors per cluster, CX = bytes per sector, DX = total clusters, and DS:BX -> the media ID byte, as the list gives; AL=FFh if DOS_GetAllocationInfo fails.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - GET ALLOCATION INFORMATION FOR SPECIFIC DRIVE
case 0x1c:      /* Get allocation info for specific drive */

entries.name: null: read-only drives
entries.description: Does nothing: it stands in for the CP/M call for the map of read-only drives.
entries.behaviour: The emulator sends it to its default case, which sets AL to 00h and logs the call as unhandled.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - NULL FUNCTION FOR CP/M COMPATIBILITY
case 0x1d:      /* NULL Function for CP/M compatibility or Extended rename FCB */

entries.name: null: file attributes
entries.description: Does nothing: it stands in for the CP/M call for setting file attributes.
entries.behaviour: The emulator sends it to its default case, which sets AL to 00h and logs the call as unhandled.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - NULL FUNCTION FOR CP/M COMPATIBILITY
case 0x1e:      /* NULL Function for CP/M compatibility or Extended rename FCB */

entries.name: null: user number
entries.description: Does nothing: it stands in for the CP/M call for getting or setting the user number.
entries.behaviour: The emulator sends it to its default case, which sets AL to 00h and logs the call as unhandled.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - NULL FUNCTION FOR CP/M COMPATIBILITY
case 0x20:      /* NULL Function for CP/M compatibility or Extended rename FCB */

entries.name: dpb default drive
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the drive parameter block of the default drive.
entries.behaviour: The emulator runs the AH=32h code with the default drive: AL=00h and DS:BX -> the block for a mounted drive that is not removable, AL=FFh otherwise.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - GET DRIVE PARAMETER BLOCK FOR DEFAULT DRIVE
case 0x1f: /* Get drive parameter block for default drive */

entries.name: fcb random read
entries.description: Reads the record at the FCB's random record number into the disk transfer area.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the opened FCB. AL is the status DOS_FCBRandomRead returns for one record: 00h successful, 01h no data, 03h partial record read. The file position is not updated.
entries.differs: The list also gives 02h, segment wrap in the DTA; the FCB helpers in src/dos/dos_files.cpp (FCB_SUCCESS, FCB_READ_NODATA, FCB_READ_PARTIAL) never return it.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - READ RANDOM RECORD FROM FCB FILE
case 0x21:      /* Read random record from FCB */

entries.name: fcb random write
entries.description: Writes the record in the disk transfer area at the FCB's random record number.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the opened FCB. AL is the status DOS_FCBRandomWrite returns for one record: 00h successful, 01h for any failure. The file position is not updated.
entries.differs: The list gives 01h as disk full and also 02h, segment wrap in the DTA; the FCB helpers in src/dos/dos_files.cpp return 01h (FCB_ERR_WRITE) for every failure and never 02h.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - WRITE RANDOM RECORD TO FCB FILE
case 0x22:      /* Write random record to FCB */

entries.name: fcb file size
entries.description: Returns the size of the file named by the unopened FCB at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: AL=00h if DOS_FCBGetFileSize succeeds and FFh if not. On success the list says the FCB's random record field holds the size in records, rounded up to a full record.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - GET FILE SIZE FOR FCB
case 0x23:      /* Get file size for FCB */

entries.name: fcb set random record
entries.description: Sets the FCB's random record number from its current record.
entries.behaviour: DS:DX points at the opened FCB. The emulator passes it to DOS_FCBSetRandomRecord; the list says the result is the random record number for the current record number and record size.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - SET RANDOM RECORD NUMBER FOR FCB
case 0x24:      /* Set Random Record number for FCB */

entries.name: set vector
entries.description: Sets the interrupt vector AL to the handler at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: AL = interrupt number, DS:DX = the new handler. The emulator stores DS:DX in the vector table with RealSetVec.

entries.name: new psp
entries.description: Creates a new program segment prefix at segment DX.
entries.behaviour: The emulator calls DOS_NewPSP with DX and the size of the current PSP, and sets AL to F0h (the list says AL is destroyed).

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - CREATE NEW PROGRAM SEGMENT PREFIX

entries.name: fcb block read
entries.description: Reads CX records from the opened FCB at DS:DX into the disk transfer area.
entries.behaviour: AL is the status DOS_FCBRandomRead returns: 00h all records read, 01h no data, 03h partial read. CX is passed by reference and returns the records read. The file position is updated.
entries.differs: The list also gives 02h, segment wrap in the DTA; the FCB helpers in src/dos/dos_files.cpp (FCB_SUCCESS, FCB_READ_NODATA, FCB_READ_PARTIAL) never return it.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - RANDOM BLOCK READ FROM FCB FILE
case 0x27:      /* Random block read from FCB */

entries.name: fcb block write
entries.description: Writes CX records from the disk transfer area to the opened FCB at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: AL is the status DOS_FCBRandomWrite returns: 00h successful, 01h for any failure. CX is passed by reference and returns the records written. The file position is updated.
entries.differs: The list gives 01h as disk full or file read-only and also 02h, segment wrap in the DTA; the FCB helpers in src/dos/dos_files.cpp return 01h (FCB_ERR_WRITE) for every failure, never 02h.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - RANDOM BLOCK WRITE TO FCB FILE
case 0x28:      /* Random Block write to FCB */

entries.name: fcb parse name
entries.description: Parses the filename at DS:SI into an unopened FCB at ES:DI.
entries.behaviour: AL = parsing options. The emulator copies up to 1023 bytes from DS:SI, parses them with FCB_Parsename, returns its result in AL (00h no wildcards, 01h wildcards, FFh invalid drive) and advances SI past what was parsed.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 1+ - PARSE FILENAME INTO FCB

entries.name: get date
entries.description: Returns the DOS system date.
entries.behaviour: CX = year, DH = month, DL = day and AL = day of week (0 = Sunday, from Zeller's congruence). The IBM PC path returns the date DOS keeps internally and reads no clock at the call.

entries.name: set date
entries.description: Sets the DOS system date and the BIOS real-time clock date.
entries.behaviour: CX = year, DH = month, DL = day. An invalid date (year outside 1980 to 9999, bad month, or a day past the month's end, leap years counted) returns AL=FFh. Otherwise the emulator sets the clock through INT 1Ah AH=05h in BCD, stores the date, returns AL=00h, and switches off host time sync if it was on.
entries.differs: The list gives the valid years as 1980 to 2099; the emulator accepts 1980 to 9999.

entries.name: get time
entries.description: Returns the DOS system time.
entries.behaviour: CH = hour, CL = minute, DH = second, DL = 1/100 seconds. The emulator reads the tick count with INT 1Ah AH=00h, adds a day when AL reports midnight, converts the ticks to time from the PIT tick rate, and adds a simulated DOS overhead.

entries.name: set time
entries.description: Sets the DOS system time and the BIOS real-time clock time.
entries.behaviour: CH = hour, CL = minute, DH = second, DL = 1/100 seconds. A value out of range (hour over 23, minute or second over 59, hundredths over 99) returns AL=FFh. Otherwise the emulator sets the clock with INT 1Ah AH=03h, sets the tick count with AH=01h, returns AL=00h, and switches off host time sync if it was on.

entries.name: set verify flag
entries.description: Turns write verification on or off.
entries.behaviour: AL=01h turns the verify flag on and any other AL turns it off.

entries.name: get dta
entries.description: Returns the address of the disk transfer area.
entries.behaviour: Returns ES:BX = the current DTA.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - GET DISK TRANSFER AREA ADDRESS

entries.name: dos version
entries.description: Returns the DOS version the emulator reports.
entries.behaviour: AL = major, AH = minor, BL=00h, CX=0000h. With AL=00h on entry, BH = FFh (Microsoft), or 29h when emulating the J-3100. With AL=01h and DOS loaded in the HMA, BH = 10h.

entries.name: keep resident
entries.description: Ends the program with return code AL, leaving DX paragraphs resident.
entries.behaviour: The emulator resizes the PSP's memory block to DX paragraphs, then terminates the program as a TSR with AL as the return code. It never returns and does not set the carry flag. If the PSP's block is marked free it is first marked allocated to the PSP.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - TERMINATE AND STAY RESIDENT

entries.name: dpb specific drive
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the drive parameter block of the drive in DL.
entries.behaviour: DL = drive (00h = default, 01h = A:). AL=00h and DS:BX -> the block for a mounted drive that is not removable; AL=FFh otherwise. The emulator fills the block's free-cluster word when it holds FFFFh.
entries.differs: The list gives FFh for an invalid or network drive; the emulator also gives it for a removable drive.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - GET DOS DRIVE PARAMETER BLOCK FOR SPECIFIC DRIVE
case 0x32: /* Get drive parameter block for specific drive */

entries.name: break checking
entries.description: Gets or sets extended break checking, among other subfunctions chosen by AL.
entries.behaviour: AL = 00h to 07h selects the subfunction; any other AL returns AL=FFh.

entries.name: get break state
entries.description: Returns the extended break checking state.
entries.behaviour: Returns DL = the break check flag the emulator holds.

entries.name: set break state
entries.description: Sets the extended break checking state.
entries.behaviour: DL = new state: the flag is set when DL is above 0. Nothing is returned.

entries.name: swap break state
entries.description: Sets the break checking state and returns the old one.
entries.behaviour: DL = new state, set when DL is above 0. Returns DL = the old state.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 3.x+ internal - GET AND SET EXTENDED CONTROL-BREAK CHECKING STATE

entries.name: get cpsw state
entries.description: Gets the code-page switching flag, a call that has been a no-op in public DOS releases.
entries.behaviour: The emulator logs an error and returns nothing; its code is shared with the set call, AL=04h.
entries.differs: The list returns DL = the current CPSW; the emulator returns nothing.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 3.4/4.0 - GET CURRENT CPSW STATE

entries.name: set cpsw state
entries.description: Sets the code-page switching flag, a call that has been a no-op in public DOS releases.
entries.behaviour: The emulator logs an error and returns nothing.

entries.name: get boot drive
entries.description: Returns the boot drive.
entries.behaviour: Returns DL = 3, which is drive C: (1 = A:); the emulator's source marks it as to be made configurable.

sources.cites: case 5:reg_dl=3;break; /* Drive C: (TODO: Make configurable, or else initially set to Z: then re-set to the first drive mounted */

entries.name: get true version
entries.description: Returns the true DOS version, which SETVER cannot change.
entries.behaviour: Returns BL = major, BH = minor, DL = revision, and DH = 10h when DOS is in the HMA, else 00h.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 5+ - GET TRUE VERSION NUMBER

entries.name: set dos_flag
entries.description: Sets or clears bit 5 of the Windows 95 DOS_FLAG.
entries.behaviour: The emulator does nothing for it.

entries.name: indos flag
entries.description: Returns the address of the InDOS flag.
entries.behaviour: Returns ES = DOS_SDA_SEG and BX = DOS_SDA_OFS + 1, the emulator's swappable data area.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - GET ADDRESS OF INDOS FLAG

entries.name: get vector
entries.description: Returns the interrupt vector AL.
entries.behaviour: Returns ES:BX = the vector, read from the interrupt vector table at AL times 4.

entries.name: free space
entries.description: Returns the free and total space of the drive in DL.
entries.behaviour: DL = drive (00h = default, 01h = A:). Returns AX = sectors per cluster, BX = free clusters, CX = bytes per sector, DX = total clusters, or AX=FFFFh for an invalid drive.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - GET FREE DISK SPACE

entries.name: switch char
entries.description: Gets or sets the switch character and the \DEV\ prefix flag, by AL.
entries.behaviour: AL = 00h to 03h selects the subfunction. For any other AL the emulator's handler changes no register.
entries.differs: The list returns AL=FFh for an unsupported subfunction; the emulator returns nothing for an AL above 03h.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2.x and 3.3+ only - "AVAILDEV" - SPECIFY \DEV\ PREFIX USE
case 0x37:      /* Get/Set Switch char Get/Set Availdev thing */

entries.name: get switch char
entries.description: Returns the character that introduces command switches.
entries.behaviour: Returns AL=00h and DL=2Fh ('/'), always.

entries.name: set switch char
entries.description: Sets the switch character.
entries.behaviour: The emulator logs the attempt, changes nothing and returns AL=00h.

entries.name: get availdev flag
entries.description: Returns whether the \DEV\ prefix of device names is optional.
entries.behaviour: Returns AL=00h and DL=FFh: the prefix is optional.

entries.name: set availdev flag
entries.description: Sets whether the \DEV\ prefix of device names is optional.
entries.behaviour: The emulator logs the attempt, changes nothing and returns AL=00h.

entries.name: country info
entries.description: Gets the country information, or sets the country code.
entries.behaviour: With AL=00h it copies the country table (0x18 bytes) to DS:DX, returns AL = country number (FFh if it is above 254) and BX = country number, CF clear. With DX=FFFFh it sets the country to AL (to BX if AL=FFh), returns AX=0, CF clear. Anything else sets CF.
entries.differs: The list defines AL=01h to FEh as a specific country and AL=FFh with BX; the emulator serves only AL=00h and DX=FFFFh, and sets CF for the rest.

entries.name: mkdir
entries.description: Creates the directory named by the ASCIZ path at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: CF clear and AX=0005h on success; CF set and AX = the DOS error code on failure. The emulator forces short names for the call.

entries.name: rmdir
entries.description: Removes the directory named by the ASCIZ path at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: CF clear and AX=0005h on success; CF set and AX = the DOS error code on failure. The emulator forces short names for the call.

entries.name: chdir
entries.description: Makes the directory named by the ASCIZ path at DS:DX the current directory.
entries.behaviour: CF clear and AX=0000h on success; CF set and AX = the DOS error code on failure.

entries.name: create file
entries.description: Creates or truncates the file named by the ASCIZ path at DS:DX, with attributes CX.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear and AX = the new file handle. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code. The emulator forces short names for the call.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - "CREAT" - CREATE OR TRUNCATE FILE
case 0x3c:      /* CREATE Create or truncate file */

entries.name: open file
entries.description: Opens the existing file named by the ASCIZ path at DS:DX, with the access mode in AL.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear and AX = the file handle. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code. The emulator tries the name as a short name first and, if that fails with long file names enabled, once more as typed.

entries.name: close file
entries.description: Closes the file handle in BX.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear; the emulator passes AL to DOS_CloseFile, which stores the handle's reference count from before the close there, so AL is changed. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

entries.name: read file
entries.description: Reads CX bytes from the handle in BX into the buffer at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear and AX = the bytes read. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code. A read that would pass the end of the 64 KB segment from an offset not a multiple of 16 is cut to 10000h minus that offset's low four bits (MS-DOS 5.0 behaviour).

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - "READ" - READ FROM FILE OR DEVICE
case 0x3f:      /* READ Read from file or device */

entries.name: write file
entries.description: Writes CX bytes from the buffer at DS:DX to the handle in BX.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear and AX = the bytes written. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code. A write past the end of the 64 KB segment is cut as AH=3Fh cuts a read; a closed handle gives error 6; 'Packed file is corrupt' written to handle 2 can be swallowed.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - "WRITE" - WRITE TO FILE OR DEVICE
case 0x40:                  /* WRITE Write to file or device */

entries.name: delete file
entries.description: Deletes the file named by the ASCIZ path at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code. The emulator forces short names for the call.

entries.name: seek
entries.description: Moves the file position of the handle in BX by the signed offset CX:DX from the origin in AL.
entries.behaviour: AL = 00h start, 01h current position, 02h end. On success CF is clear and DX:AX = the new position. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - "LSEEK" - SET CURRENT FILE POSITION
case 0x42:                  /* LSEEK Set current file position */

entries.name: file attributes
entries.description: Gets (AL=00h) or sets (AL=01h) the attributes of the file named by the ASCIZ path at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: Any other AL logs an error, returns AX=0001h and sets CF.

entries.name: get attributes
entries.description: Returns the attributes of the file named by the ASCIZ path at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear, CX = the attributes and AX = the same value (undocumented in the emulator's source). On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

entries.name: set attributes
entries.description: Sets the attributes of the file named by the ASCIZ path at DS:DX to CX.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear and AX = 0202h (destroyed). On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

entries.name: ioctl
entries.description: Device control: AL selects the subfunction, BX holds the handle.
entries.behaviour: The emulator hands the call to DOS_IOCTL. CF is clear on success; on failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

entries.name: dup handle
entries.description: Duplicates the file handle in BX.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear and AX = the new handle. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

entries.name: dup2
entries.description: Makes the handle in CX a duplicate of the handle in BX, closing CX if open.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear and AX = CX, which the emulator's source notes not all sources agree on. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.
entries.differs: The list returns no value in AX; the emulator returns AX = CX.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - "DUP2", "FORCEDUP" - FORCE DUPLICATE FILE HANDLE
case 0x46:                  /* DUP2,FORCEDUP Force duplicate file handle */

entries.name: get cwd
entries.description: Returns the current directory of the drive in DL.
entries.behaviour: DL = drive (00h = default, 01h = A:), DS:SI -> buffer. On success the emulator writes the ASCIZ path there, CF is clear and AX=0100h. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

entries.name: alloc memory
entries.description: Allocates BX paragraphs of memory.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear and AX = the segment of the block. On failure CF is set, AX = the DOS error code and BX = the size of the largest available block.

entries.name: free memory
entries.description: Frees the memory block at segment ES.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

entries.name: resize memory
entries.description: Resizes the block at segment ES to BX paragraphs.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear and AX = ES. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code; BX = the largest size available, except after error 7, when it is not changed.

entries.name: exec
entries.description: Loads and optionally runs a program: AL = type, DS:DX = ASCIZ program name, ES:BX = parameter block.
entries.behaviour: The emulator passes the name, the parameter block and AL to DOS_Execute. If it fails, CF is set and AX = the DOS error code. On success it records the program name and command tail of the running program.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - "EXEC" - LOAD AND/OR EXECUTE PROGRAM
case 0x4b:                  /* EXEC Load and/or execute program */

entries.name: exit
entries.description: Ends the program with return code AL.
entries.behaviour: The emulator terminates the current PSP with AL as the return code, clears the running program's name and arguments, and sets AX=3E01h for the parent, as the source comment says real MS-DOS appears to return on leaving AH=4Bh.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - "EXIT" - TERMINATE WITH RETURN CODE
case 0x4c:                  /* EXIT Terminate with return code */

entries.name: get return code
entries.description: Returns the return code and the termination type of the last child.
entries.behaviour: Returns AL = return code and AH = termination type, CF clear. The emulator keeps both and does not clear them.
entries.differs: The list says the stored return code is cleared once read; the emulator's handler does not clear it.

entries.name: find first
entries.description: Finds the first file matching the ASCIZ spec at DS:DX with attribute mask CX.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear and AX=0000h (undocumented), and the DTA holds the find data. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code; unless long names are on, a bad path is reported first.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - "FINDFIRST" - FIND FIRST MATCHING FILE
case 0x4e: {                /* FINDFIRST Find first matching file */

entries.name: find next
entries.description: Finds the next file of the search the DTA holds.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear and AX=0000h (undocumented). On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ - "FINDNEXT" - FIND NEXT MATCHING FILE
case 0x4f:                  /* FINDNEXT Find next matching file */

entries.name: set psp
entries.description: Sets the current process, by the segment of its PSP in BX.
entries.behaviour: The emulator stores BX as the current PSP segment.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ internal - SET CURRENT PROCESS ID (SET PSP ADDRESS)

entries.name: get psp
entries.description: Returns the segment of the current process's PSP.
entries.behaviour: Returns BX = the current PSP segment.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ internal - GET CURRENT PROCESS ID (GET PSP ADDRESS)

entries.name: list of lists
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the DOS list of lists.
entries.behaviour: Returns ES:BX = the emulator's DOS info block. Before returning it sets the block's device count to 2 floppies plus the run of mounted non-removable drives from C: on.

sources.cites: INT 21 U - DOS 2+ internal - "SYSVARS" - GET LIST OF LISTS

entries.name: bpb to dpb
entries.description: Translates the BIOS parameter block at DS:SI into the drive parameter block at ES:BP.
entries.behaviour: The emulator fills the block's sector, cluster, FAT, root directory, first data sector, highest cluster and media fields from the BPB, in the DOS 4+ layout or the earlier one by the version it reports, sets the free-cluster search start to 0 and the free clusters to FFFFh (unknown), and returns no error.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ internal - TRANSLATE BIOS PARAMETER BLOCK TO DRIVE PARAM BLOCK
case 0x53:                  /* Translate BIOS parameter block to drive parameter block */

entries.name: get verify flag
entries.description: Returns the state of the verify flag.
entries.behaviour: Returns AL=01h if the emulator's verify flag is on, else 00h.

entries.name: child psp
entries.description: Creates a child program segment prefix at segment DX.
entries.behaviour: SI = the value for the memory size field. The emulator calls DOS_ChildPSP with DX and SI, makes DX the current PSP, and sets AL to F0h (destroyed).

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2+ internal - CREATE CHILD PSP

entries.name: rename
entries.description: Renames the file or directory named by the ASCIZ path at DS:DX to the ASCIZ path at ES:DI.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code. The emulator forces short names for the call.

entries.name: file time
entries.description: Gets (AL=00h) or sets (AL=01h) the time and date stamps of the file handle in BX.
entries.behaviour: AL=00h returns CX and DX, CF clear; AL=01h sets them from CX and DX. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code. Any other AL is logged and changes nothing.

sources.cites: case 0x57:                  /* Get/Set File's Date and Time */

entries.name: alloc strategy
entries.description: Gets or sets the memory allocation strategy, or the UMB link state, by AL.
entries.behaviour: AL = 00h to 03h selects the subfunction. Any other AL logs an error, returns AX=0001h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 2.11+ - GET OR SET MEMORY ALLOCATION STRATEGY

entries.name: get alloc strategy
entries.description: Returns the memory allocation strategy.
entries.behaviour: Returns AX = DOS_GetMemAllocStrategy and CF clear.

entries.name: set alloc strategy
entries.description: Sets the memory allocation strategy to BX.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear; if DOS_SetMemAllocStrategy refuses BX, AX=0001h and CF is set.

entries.name: get umb link
entries.description: Returns whether the upper memory blocks are linked into the DOS memory chain.
entries.behaviour: Returns AL = 01h if linked, else 00h, and CF clear.

entries.name: set umb link
entries.description: Links the upper memory blocks into the DOS memory chain, or unlinks them, by BX.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear; if DOS_LinkUMBsToMemChain refuses BX, AX=0001h and CF is set.

entries.name: extended error
entries.description: Returns the extended information of the last DOS error.
entries.behaviour: Returns AX = the last error code, BH = 08h (not found) for file not found and path not found, else 00h (unspecified), BL = 01h (retry), CH = 00h (unknown locus), CF clear. BX on entry is ignored.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 3.0+ - GET EXTENDED ERROR INFORMATION

entries.name: create temp file
entries.description: Creates a file with a unique name in the directory the ASCIZ path at DS:DX names.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear, AX = the file handle and the generated name is written back at DS:DX. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code. CX is not read.
entries.differs: The list takes the attributes in CX; the emulator's handler does not pass CX to DOS_CreateTempFile.

entries.name: create new file
entries.description: Creates the file named by the ASCIZ path at DS:DX, failing if it exists.
entries.behaviour: CX = attributes. If the file can be opened, the emulator closes it and fails with error 80. Otherwise CF is clear and AX = the handle, or on failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

entries.name: record locking
entries.description: Locks (AL=00h) or unlocks (AL=01h) a region of the file handle in BX.
entries.behaviour: CX:DX = start offset, SI:DI = length. If the emulator's file sharing is not enabled it fails with error 1; otherwise DOS_LockFile decides, and on success AX=0 and CF is clear. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

entries.name: network functions
entries.description: Remote server call (AL=00h) or get the swappable data area (AL=06h).
entries.behaviour: AL=00h loads AX, BX, CX, DX, SI, DI, DS and ES from the register block at DS:DX and runs the handler again. AL=06h returns DS:SI -> the DOS data area, CX = its swap size, DX = 001Ah, CF clear. Any other AL is logged as unsupported.

entries.name: network printer fns
entries.description: Gets the machine name (AL=00h) when a network redirector is available.
entries.behaviour: On success it writes the host name, padded with spaces to 15 characters, at DS:DX, returns CX=01FFh and clears CF. If AL is not 00h, or no redirector answers, it returns AL=01h and sets CF.

entries.name: network redirection
entries.description: Network redirection calls, selected by AL.
entries.behaviour: The emulator returns AX=0001h and sets CF (failure). Only Windows builds serve a few named-pipe subfunctions first.

entries.name: truename
entries.description: Canonicalizes the ASCIZ name at DS:SI into the 128-byte buffer at ES:DI.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear and the canonical ASCIZ name is written at ES:DI. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 3.0+ - "TRUENAME" - CANONICALIZE FILENAME OR PATH

entries.name: unused network
entries.description: Does nothing: reserved for network use.
entries.behaviour: The emulator sends it to its default case, which sets AL to 00h.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 3.0+ - UNUSED (RESERVED FOR NETWORK USE)

entries.name: get psp
entries.description: Returns the segment of the current process's PSP.
entries.behaviour: Returns BX = the current PSP segment.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 3.0+ - GET CURRENT PSP ADDRESS

entries.name: get dbcs table
entries.description: Returns the double-byte character set table.
entries.behaviour: With AL=00h and a table present: DS:SI -> the table (offset 2 past its start), AL=00h, CF clear. Otherwise AL=FFh and CF is untouched.

entries.name: driver lookahead
entries.description: Sets the device driver lookahead flag.
entries.behaviour: The emulator logs the call and does nothing.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 3.2+ internal - SET DEVICE DRIVER LOOKAHEAD FLAG
case 0x64:                  /* Set device driver lookahead flag */

entries.name: extended country info
entries.description: Returns extended country information or capitalizes text, by AL.
entries.behaviour: With CX below 5, AL up to 07h fails with error 1 and CF set. AL = 01h to 07h returns country information or a table pointer at ES:DI; AL = 20h to 23h capitalizes or classifies a character. Any other AL stops the emulator with an error.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 3.3+ - GET EXTENDED COUNTRY INFORMATION
case 0x65:                  /* Get extended country information and a lot of other useless shit*/

entries.name: get intl info
entries.description: Returns the general internationalization information at ES:DI.
entries.behaviour: ES:DI gets AL, then 0026h, then the country number; if CX > 6 the loaded code page follows, and if CX > 8 the country table is copied after it, with CX returned as at most 29h. CF is clear. With CX below 5 it fails: error 1, CF set.

entries.name: filename term table
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the filename terminator table.
entries.behaviour: Writes AL and a far pointer to the table at ES:DI and returns CX=5, CF clear. With CX below 5 it fails: error 1, CF set.

sources.cites: case 0x05: // Get pointer to filename terminator table

entries.name: uppercase table
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the uppercase table.
entries.behaviour: Writes AL and a far pointer to the table at ES:DI (an identity table in UTF-8 names mode) and returns CX=5, CF clear. With CX below 5 it fails: error 1, CF set.

sources.cites: case 0x02: // Get pointer to uppercase table

entries.name: filename upcase table
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the filename uppercase table.
entries.behaviour: Writes AL and a far pointer to the table at ES:DI (an identity table in UTF-8 names mode) and returns CX=5, CF clear. It is the same code as AL=02h. With CX below 5 it fails: error 1, CF set.

sources.cites: case 0x04: // Get pointer to filename uppercase table

entries.name: collating table
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the collating sequence table.
entries.behaviour: Writes AL and a far pointer to the table at ES:DI and returns CX=5, CF clear. With CX below 5 it fails: error 1, CF set.

sources.cites: case 0x06: // Get pointer to collating sequence table

entries.name: lowercase table
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the lowercase table.
entries.behaviour: The emulator returns the double-byte character set table where one exists: AL and its far pointer at ES:DI, CX=5, CF clear. Without one it writes nothing and leaves CF alone. With CX below 5 it fails: error 1, CF set.
entries.differs: The list says AL=03h returns the lowercase table; the emulator shares the code of AL=07h and returns the double-byte table.

sources.cites: case 0x03: // Get pointer to lowercase table

entries.name: dbcs table
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the double-byte character set table.
entries.behaviour: Writes AL and a far pointer to the table at ES:DI and returns CX=5, CF clear, when a table exists; otherwise it writes nothing and leaves CF alone. With CX below 5 it fails: error 1, CF set.

sources.cites: case 0x07: // Get pointer to double byte char set table

entries.name: capitalize char
entries.description: Capitalizes the character in DL.
entries.behaviour: Returns DL = the uppercase character, CF clear. In UTF-8 names mode a character from 80h up is left as it is.

entries.name: capitalize string
entries.description: Capitalizes the CX characters at DS:DX in place.
entries.behaviour: CF is clear. A length over the emulator's copy buffer stops the emulator with an error. In UTF-8 names mode a character from 80h up is left as it is.

entries.name: capitalize asciiz
entries.description: Capitalizes the ASCIZ string at DS:DX in place.
entries.behaviour: CF is clear. A string over the emulator's copy buffer stops the emulator with an error. In UTF-8 names mode a character from 80h up is left as it is.

entries.name: yes/no character
entries.description: Classifies the character in DL as yes, no or neither.
entries.behaviour: Returns AX = 1 if DL, lowercased, is the yes character, 0 if it is the no character, 2 otherwise, CF clear. FORMAT.COM and FDISK.EXE rely on it.

sources.cites: INT 21 U - DOS 4.0+ - DETERMINE IF CHARACTER REPRESENTS YES/NO RESPONSE
case 0x23: /* Determine if character represents yes/no response (MS-DOS 4.0+) */

entries.name: code page table
entries.description: Gets (AL=01h) or sets (AL=02h) the global code page.
entries.behaviour: Any other AL sets error 1: AX=0001h and CF set.

sources.cites: case 0x66:                  /* Get/Set global code page table  */

entries.name: get code page
entries.description: Returns the active and the system code page.
entries.behaviour: Returns BX = DX = the loaded code page, CF clear.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 3.3+ - GET GLOBAL CODE PAGE TABLE

entries.name: set code page
entries.description: Sets the active code page to BX.
entries.behaviour: It works only with TrueType output, a supported code page, and a machine that is not PC-98, JEGA or DOS/V; otherwise AX=0002h and CF is set. On success the emulator reloads its language, fonts and drives and CF is clear.

sources.cites: INT 21 - DOS 3.3+ - SET GLOBAL CODE PAGE TABLE

entries.name: set handle count
entries.description: Sets the size of the process's file handle table to BX.
entries.behaviour: On success CF is clear; otherwise AX = the error PSP.SetNumFiles returns and CF is set.

entries.name: commit file
entries.description: Writes the buffered data of a file to disk.
entries.behaviour: The emulator flushes the handle in BL, not BX. On success AH=68h and CF is clear. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.
entries.differs: The list takes the handle in BX; the emulator's handler reads it from BL.

entries.name: disk serial number
entries.description: Gets (AL=00h) or sets (AL=01h) the serial number of the disk in BL.
entries.behaviour: The emulator rewrites the call as the generic block device IOCTL (AX=440Dh, CH=08h, CL=66h to get, 46h to set), runs it, and restores CX. Any other AL stops the emulator with an error.

sources.cites: INT 21 U - DOS 4.0+ internal - GET/SET DISK SERIAL NUMBER

entries.name: get serial number
entries.description: Gets the disk serial number.
entries.behaviour: The emulator turns it into the IOCTL AX=440Dh with CH=08h and CL=66h and runs it, then restores CX.

entries.name: set serial number
entries.description: Sets the disk serial number.
entries.behaviour: The emulator turns it into the IOCTL AX=440Dh with CH=08h and CL=46h and runs it, then restores CX.

entries.name: commit file 6Ah
entries.description: Writes the buffered data of a file to disk, as AH=68h.
entries.behaviour: The emulator runs the AH=68h code: it flushes the handle in BL, then AH=68h and CF clear on success.

entries.name: null function
entries.description: Does nothing.
entries.behaviour: The emulator sends it to its default case, which sets AL to 00h.

entries.name: extended open
entries.description: Opens or creates the file named by the ASCIZ path at DS:SI.
entries.behaviour: BX = mode, CX = attributes and DX = action go to DOS_OpenFileExtended. On success CF is clear, AX = the handle, and CX is also set by DOS_OpenFileExtended. On failure CF is set and AX = the DOS error code.

entries.name: find first rom
entries.description: Finds the first ROM program: not implemented.
entries.behaviour: The emulator logs that it is not implemented and sends it to its default case, which sets AL to 00h.

sources.cites: INT 21 U - DOS 5+ ROM - FIND FIRST ROM PROGRAM
case 0x6d:                  /* ROM - Find first ROM program */

entries.name: find next rom
entries.description: Finds the next ROM program: not implemented.
entries.behaviour: The emulator logs that it is not implemented and sends it to its default case, which sets AL to 00h.

sources.cites: INT 21 U - DOS 5+ ROM - FIND NEXT ROM PROGRAM
case 0x6e:                  /* ROM - Find next ROM program */

entries.name: rom functions
entries.description: ROM functions: not implemented.
entries.behaviour: The emulator logs that it is not implemented and sends it to its default case, which sets AL to 00h.

entries.name: long filename fns
entries.description: Windows 95 long file name functions, selected by AL.
entries.behaviour: With long file names off the emulator returns AX=7100h and sets CF. If the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode it returns AX=0002h and sets CF. An AL it has no routine for returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

entries.name: lfn mkdir
entries.description: Makes a directory from the ASCIZ long name at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_7139 routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - MAKE DIRECTORY

entries.name: lfn rmdir
entries.description: Removes the directory named by the ASCIZ long name at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_713a routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - REMOVE DIRECTORY

entries.name: lfn chdir
entries.description: Makes the directory named by the ASCIZ long name at DS:DX current.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_713b routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - CHANGE DIRECTORY

entries.name: lfn delete
entries.description: Deletes the file named by the ASCIZ long name at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_7141 routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - DELETE FILE

entries.name: lfn attributes
entries.description: Gets or sets the extended attributes of the file named at DS:DX.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_7143 routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - EXTENDED GET/SET FILE ATTRIBUTES

entries.name: lfn get cwd
entries.description: Returns the current directory of the drive in DL.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_7147 routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - GET CURRENT DIRECTORY

entries.name: lfn find first
entries.description: Finds the first file matching a long-name spec.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_714e routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - FIND FIRST MATCHING FILE

entries.name: lfn find next
entries.description: Finds the next file of the search the handle in BX names.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_714f routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - FIND NEXT MATCHING FILE

entries.name: lfn rename
entries.description: Renames a file or directory; long names are allowed.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_7156 routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - RENAME FILE

entries.name: lfn create or open
entries.description: Creates or opens a file by long name.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_716c routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - CREATE OR OPEN FILE

entries.name: lfn volume info
entries.description: Returns information about the volume whose root the ASCIZ name at DS:DX gives.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_71a0 routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - GET VOLUME INFORMATION

entries.name: lfn find close
entries.description: Ends the directory search the handle in BX names.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_71a1 routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - "FindClose" - TERMINATE DIRECTORY SEARCH

entries.name: lfn file info by handle
entries.description: Returns information about the file handle in BX.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_71a6 routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - GET FILE INFO BY HANDLE

entries.name: lfn short name
entries.description: Generates a short filename from the long one at DS:SI.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_71a8 routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - GENERATE SHORT FILENAME

entries.name: lfn truename
entries.description: Canonicalizes a path, or gets the short or long form of a name, by CL.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_7160 routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - "TRUENAME" - CANONICALIZE PATH

entries.name: lfn time convert
entries.description: Converts between a file time and a DOS time, by BL.
entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_71a7 routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - FILE TIME TO DOS TIME

entries.behaviour: With long file names on, the emulator runs its DOS_Int21_71aa routine, unless the name is not valid UTF-8 in UTF-8 mode, which returns AX=0002h with CF set. With them off it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - CREATE SUBST

entries.name: lfn server create
entries.description: Creates or opens a file by long name, for a network server.
entries.behaviour: The emulator treats it as unimplemented: it returns AX=7100h and sets CF.

sources.cites: INT 21 - Windows95 - LONG FILENAME - SERVER CREATE OR OPEN FILE

entries.name: fat32 and drive calls
entries.description: MS-DOS 7 drive locking and flushing, and the FAT32 calls, by AL.
entries.behaviour: Below DOS 7 it returns AX=7300h and sets CF. AL=00h with CL below 2 returns AL=CL, AH=00h, CF clear; AL=02h returns the extended DPB of a FAT32 drive, AL=03h the extended free space, and AL=05h with CX=FFFFh (DOS 7.10+) a FAT32 disk read or write. Anything else sets CF and AX=FFFFh.

sources.cites: INT 21 - MS-DOS 7 - DRIVE LOCKING AND FLUSHING

entries.name: unhandled e0h
entries.description: An AH value the emulator lists by itself and handles as an unhandled call.
entries.behaviour: It falls to the emulator's default case, which sets AL to 00h.

entries.name: ancient art cga
entries.description: An AH value the emulator's source names as used by Ancient Art Of War in its CGA version.
entries.behaviour: It falls to the emulator's default case, which sets AL to 00h.
